cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Cinque Terre
tagline: Five pastel villages on the cliffs
summary: Five fishing villages cling to the cliffs of the Ligurian coast, linked by a train line and hiking trails through vineyards. Colourful houses tumble down to tiny harbours, and the food is all pesto, focaccia and anchovies.
seasonNote: April to June and September to October are best. July and August are very crowded and hot. Many trails close after heavy rain, and some places close in winter.
arrival: Trains from La Spezia link all five villages in minutes; La Spezia is about 2.5 hours from Florence and 3 hours from Milan.
gettingAround: The Cinque Terre Card covers the local trains and the paid trails; ferries run between villages in good weather.
foodTip: Trofie with pesto, focaccia, fried anchovies and the sweet Sciacchetrà wine.
buyTip: Pesto, local olive oil, lemon products and Sciacchetrà.
baseArea: Monterosso or Vernazza, or La Spezia for cheaper stays

items.name: Vernazza
items.summary: A tiny harbour village with a castle tower and a church on the water.
items.tip: Watch the sunset from the Doria Castle tower.

items.name: Manarola
items.summary: Pastel houses stacked on a rocky point above swimming rocks.
items.expect: The classic photo spot is on the path to Punta Bonfiglio.
items.tip: Swim off the rocks in summer.

items.name: Riomaggiore
items.summary: A steep village of tower houses around a tiny harbour.
items.tip: Climb to the castle for the view down.

items.name: Monterosso al Mare
items.summary: The largest village, with the only real sandy beach.
items.tip: Swim and lunch here.
items.why: Beach day in the Cinque Terre.

items.name: Corniglia
items.summary: The only village on a hilltop, 382 steps above the station.
items.tip: Take the shuttle bus up if you're tired.

items.name: Coastal trail (Sentiero Azzurro)
items.summary: The famous cliff path between the villages through vines and olive groves.
items.expect: Some sections need the Cinque Terre Card; check which are open.
items.tip: Hike Monterosso to Vernazza early in the morning.
items.why: The best way to see the coast.

items.name: Porto Venere
items.summary: A colourful harbour town with a church on a rock at the tip of the gulf.
items.expect: Ferries from the villages and La Spezia.
items.tip: Visit the church of San Pietro on the point.

items.name: Trofie al pesto
items.summary: Twisted fresh pasta with basil pesto, potatoes and green beans.
items.tip: Pair with a glass of local white.

items.name: Focaccia
items.summary: Oily, salty Ligurian flatbread, plain or with onions or cheese.
items.tip: Try focaccia di Recco with cheese.

items.name: Monterosso anchovies
items.summary: Fried, salted or marinated anchovies, the village's famous catch.
items.expect: Cones of fried fish sold to take away.
items.tip: Try a fritto misto cone by the beach.

cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Lake Como
tagline: Villas and mountains on an Alpine lake
summary: Lake Como is a deep, narrow lake ringed by mountains, with grand villas and gardens on its shores. Ferries link the lovely towns of Bellagio, Varenna and Como, and it's only an hour from Milan.
seasonNote: April to June and September to October are ideal, with gardens in bloom in spring. Summer is busy. Many hotels and villas close from November to March.
arrival: Trains from Milan reach Como in about 40 minutes and Varenna in about an hour.
gettingAround: Ferries are the best way between towns; buy a day pass for the central lake.
foodTip: Risotto with perch, missoltini (dried shad), polenta and Lombard cheeses.
buyTip: Como silk scarves and ties, olive oil and limoncello.

items.name: Bellagio
items.summary: The 'pearl of the lake', with stepped lanes on the point where the lake splits.
items.tip: Walk to the tip, Punta Spartivento.

items.name: Villa del Balbianello
items.summary: A villa and terraced gardens on a wooded point, seen in Star Wars and Casino Royale.
items.expect: Reached by boat taxi or a 1 km walk; closed some days.
items.tip: Book ahead; take the boat taxi from Lenno.

items.name: Villa Carlotta
items.summary: A villa with Canova sculptures and huge botanical gardens.
items.expect: Best in April and May for azaleas.
items.tip: Visit in spring.

items.name: Varenna
items.summary: A pastel fishing village with a lakeside walkway and gardens.
items.tip: Walk the Passeggiata degli Innamorati.

items.name: Villa Monastero
items.summary: A former convent with a long botanical garden along the shore.
items.tip: Walk the garden to the end.

items.name: Como Cathedral
items.summary: A marble cathedral mixing Gothic and Renaissance styles in the old town.
items.tip: Walk the walled old town afterwards.

items.name: Brunate funicular
items.summary: A funicular up to Brunate for views over the lake and Alps.
items.tip: Walk up to the Volta lighthouse.

items.name: Risotto with perch
items.summary: Risotto topped with butter-fried perch fillets from the lake.
items.tip: Order it with a lake view.

items.name: Missoltini
items.summary: Dried, salted lake shad grilled and served with polenta.
items.tip: Try it with a glass of local red.

items.name: Polenta and cheese
items.summary: Hearty polenta with melted mountain cheeses.
items.tip: Try polenta taragna.

cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Palermo · Sicily
summary: Sicily's capital is a crossroads of Greek, Arab, Norman and Spanish history, with golden mosaics in the Palatine Chapel and Monreale, grand Baroque squares and chaotic street markets. It's one of Italy's great street-food cities.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are warm and pleasant. July and August are hot. Winter is mild and quiet.
arrival: Palermo Airport is 40 minutes from the centre by train or bus. Overnight ferries come from Naples and Genoa; flights from Rome take about an hour.
gettingAround: The old centre is walkable; buses and trains reach Monreale and Cefalù.
foodTip: Arancine, panelle, pane con la milza, cannoli and granita with brioche.
buyTip: Ceramics, Sicilian puppets, almond pastries and Marsala wine.
baseArea: Old centre near the Quattro Canti

items.name: Palermo Cathedral
items.summary: A cathedral layered with Norman, Gothic and Baroque styles, with royal tombs and rooftop walks.
items.expect: Free; a fee for the roof and treasury.
items.tip: Walk the rooftops for city views.
items.why: A symbol of Palermo's mixed history.

items.name: Palatine Chapel
items.summary: A royal chapel covered in golden Byzantine mosaics under an Arab wooden ceiling.
items.expect: Inside the Norman Palace; queues at weekends.
items.tip: Book a timed ticket.
items.why: One of the world's most beautiful chapels.

items.name: Monreale Cathedral
items.summary: A hilltop cathedral with 6,000 square metres of gold mosaics and a cloister.
items.tip: See the cloister and climb the terraces.

items.name: Ballarò market
items.summary: A noisy, colourful street market of fish, fruit and street food.
items.expect: Mornings are busiest; mind your bags.
items.tip: Graze on panelle and arancine as you go.

items.name: Quattro Canti
items.summary: A Baroque crossroads of four curved façades, next to the Fontana Pretoria.
items.tip: See the nude statues of Fontana Pretoria.
items.why: The centre of the old city.

items.name: Teatro Massimo
items.summary: Italy's largest opera house, seen in The Godfather Part III.
items.expect: Guided tours by day; operas in season.
items.tip: See a performance if you can.

items.name: Cefalù
items.summary: A seaside town with a Norman cathedral under a great rock.
items.tip: Swim, then climb La Rocca.

items.name: Arancine
items.summary: Fried rice balls filled with ragù or butter and ham.
items.tip: Try both ragù and burro.

items.name: Pane con la milza
items.summary: A bun stuffed with fried veal spleen and lung, with lemon or cheese.
items.tip: Order it 'maritata', with cheese.

items.name: Cannoli
items.summary: Crisp pastry tubes filled with sweet ricotta.
items.expect: Filled fresh to order in good shops.
items.tip: Ask for it filled while you wait.

cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Bologna
tagline: Italy's food capital under red porticoes
summary: Bologna is a red-brick university city with 40 km of covered porticoes, leaning medieval towers and Europe's oldest university. It's the home of tortellini, tagliatelle al ragù and mortadella, and the gateway to Parma and Modena.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best. Summer is hot and some restaurants close in August. Winter is foggy but good for food.
arrival: High-speed trains reach Bologna from Florence (35 minutes), Milan (1 hour) and Rome (2 hours 15 minutes). The airport is 20 minutes away by Marconi Express.
gettingAround: Walk under the porticoes; buses cover the rest.
foodTip: Tagliatelle al ragù, tortellini in broth, mortadella and lasagne verde.
buyTip: Parmigiano Reggiano, balsamic vinegar from Modena and fresh pasta.

items.name: Piazza Maggiore
items.summary: A grand square with the Neptune Fountain and the huge Basilica of San Petronio.
items.expect: The basilica is free; a fee for the terrace.
items.tip: Climb San Petronio's terrace.

items.name: Two Towers
items.summary: Two leaning medieval towers, the Asinelli and the Garisenda.
items.expect: The Asinelli tower may be closed for repairs; check first.
items.tip: See them from Strada Maggiore.

items.name: Archiginnasio and Anatomical Theatre
items.summary: The old university's main building, with a wooden anatomical theatre.
items.tip: See the walls covered in coats of arms.

items.name: Santo Stefano
items.summary: A cluster of seven linked churches known as the 'Seven Churches'.
items.tip: Sit in the piazza outside with an aperitivo.

items.name: Sanctuary of San Luca
items.wiki: Sanctuary of the Madonna di San Luca
items.summary: A hilltop church reached by the world's longest portico, 666 arches.
items.expect: About an hour's walk up; a train runs too.
items.tip: Walk up, ride down.

items.name: Porticoes of Bologna
items.summary: A World Heritage network of covered walkways through the city.
items.tip: Walk Via Zamboni through the university district.

items.name: Modena
items.summary: Home of balsamic vinegar, Ferrari and a Romanesque cathedral.
items.tip: Visit an acetaia for a balsamic tasting.

items.name: Tagliatelle al ragù
items.summary: Egg pasta ribbons with slow-cooked meat sauce, the real 'Bolognese'.
items.tip: Order it in a traditional osteria.

items.name: Tortellini in brodo
items.summary: Tiny filled pasta in rich broth.
items.tip: Try it at a trattoria that makes pasta by hand.

items.name: Mortadella and cheese boards
items.summary: Silky mortadella, Parma ham and Parmigiano in the old market lanes.
items.tip: Order a tagliere with a glass of Lambrusco.

cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Verona
tagline: Romeo and Juliet's city and a Roman arena
summary: Verona is a graceful city on a bend of the Adige river, with a Roman arena that still hosts opera, medieval squares and the balcony tied to Romeo and Juliet. Lake Garda is half an hour away.
seasonNote: The opera festival in the Arena runs from June to early September. Spring and autumn are quieter; the Vinitaly wine fair fills hotels in April.
arrival: Trains reach Verona from Venice (1 hour 10 minutes) and Milan (1 hour 15 minutes). The airport is 20 minutes away.
gettingAround: The centre is compact and walkable.
foodTip: Risotto all'Amarone, bollito misto with pearà sauce, and pandoro at Christmas.
buyTip: Amarone and Valpolicella wine, Soave and local olive oil.

items.name: Verona Arena
items.summary: A 2,000-year-old Roman amphitheatre that still hosts opera under the stars.
items.expect: Summer opera tickets sell out; bring a cushion for the stone seats.
items.tip: See an opera on a summer night.

items.name: Juliet's House
items.summary: A medieval house with the famous balcony and a bronze statue of Juliet.
items.expect: The courtyard is free but crowded; the house is ticketed.
items.tip: Go first thing in the morning.

items.name: Piazza delle Erbe
items.summary: A lively square on the old Roman forum, with frescoed houses and a market.
items.tip: Have a spritz here at aperitivo time.

items.name: Torre dei Lamberti
items.summary: An 84 m medieval tower with views over the red rooftops.
items.expect: A lift goes most of the way.
items.tip: Go at sunset.
items.why: The best view of the city.

items.name: Castelvecchio
items.summary: A red-brick fortress and museum with a battlemented bridge.
items.expect: The bridge is free to walk.
items.tip: Walk the bridge for river views.

items.name: Ponte Pietra and Castel San Pietro
items.summary: A Roman bridge leading to a hill with a funicular and city views.
items.tip: Climb to Castel San Pietro for sunset.

items.name: Sirmione on Lake Garda
items.summary: A castle town on a narrow peninsula in Lake Garda, with Roman ruins and hot springs.
items.expect: About 40 minutes by bus or train and bus.
items.tip: See the Grotte di Catullo Roman villa.

items.name: Risotto all'Amarone
items.summary: A rich red risotto cooked with Amarone wine.
items.tip: Pair it with a glass of the same wine.

items.name: Bollito misto with pearà
items.summary: Boiled meats with pearà, a peppery bread-and-marrow sauce.
items.tip: Try it in winter.

items.name: Spritz aperitivo
items.summary: A spritz with snacks in the square at sunset.
items.tip: Try a spritz with Select, the Venetian bitter.

cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Dolomites · Val Gardena
tagline: Jagged pink peaks and alpine meadows
summary: The Dolomites are a World Heritage range of pale limestone towers that glow pink at sunset. From Ortisei in Val Gardena, cable cars rise to the Seceda ridge and the Alpe di Siusi meadows, and lakes and peaks like Braies and the Tre Cime are a drive away. In winter it's one of Europe's great ski areas.
seasonNote: Mid-June to September is hiking season, when lifts and huts open. December to March is ski season. Lifts close in spring and late autumn.
arrival: Fly to Venice, Verona or Innsbruck; drive about 2 to 3 hours. Trains reach Bolzano, then buses climb to Val Gardena.
gettingAround: A car gives most freedom; a dense network of buses and cable cars covers the valleys.
foodTip: Canederli (bread dumplings), speck, apple strudel and hearty dishes in mountain huts.
buyTip: Wood carvings from Val Gardena, speck and local schnapps.
baseArea: Ortisei or Selva in Val Gardena

items.name: Seceda
items.summary: A dramatic ridge of tilted peaks above green meadows, reached by cable car.
items.expect: Lifts run in summer and winter.
items.tip: Go early for clear views.

items.name: Alpe di Siusi
items.summary: Europe's largest high alpine meadow, below the Sassolungo peaks.
items.expect: A cable car from Ortisei or Siusi; cars are restricted.
items.tip: Walk between huts for lunch.

items.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
items.summary: Three giant rock towers circled by a classic loop trail.
items.expect: A toll road to the Auronzo hut; about 1.5 hours by car.
items.tip: Walk the loop anticlockwise.

items.name: Lago di Braies
items.summary: A turquoise lake below cliffs, with wooden rowing boats.
items.expect: Access and parking are limited in summer; book ahead.
items.tip: Arrive at sunrise or walk the lake loop.

items.name: Sella Pass
items.summary: A high road pass with views of the Sassolungo and Sella massif.
items.expect: Part of the Sella Ronda ski loop.
items.tip: Drive the four-pass loop in summer.

items.name: Val di Funes
items.summary: A quiet valley where Santa Maddalena church sits below the Odle peaks.
items.expect: The viewpoint is a short walk from the village.
items.tip: Go at sunset.

items.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo
items.summary: A glamorous mountain town and Winter Olympic host.
items.tip: Ride the Tofana cable car.

items.name: Canederli
items.summary: Bread dumplings with speck or cheese, in broth or with butter.
items.tip: Try the spinach ones.

items.name: Speck board
items.summary: Smoked ham with mountain cheese and rye bread.
items.tip: Pair with a local Lagrein wine.

items.name: Apple strudel
items.summary: Warm apple strudel with cream, eaten on a hut terrace.
items.expect: Every mountain hut has its own.
items.tip: Order it after a hike.
items.why: The best reward after a walk.

cashTip: Cards work in most places, but carry some euros for small cafés, markets and tourist taxes; a cover charge (coperto) on restaurant bills is normal.
name: Puglia · Alberobello & Polignano
tagline: Trulli, white towns and the Adriatic
summary: Puglia, the heel of Italy, has cone-roofed trulli houses, white hill towns, cliff-top swimming and olive groves to the horizon. Its food is simple and superb, and Baroque Lecce and the cave city of Matera are within reach.
seasonNote: May, June, September and October are ideal. July and August are hot and busy with Italian holidaymakers. Winter is quiet and many places close.
arrival: Fly to Bari or Brindisi. Trains run from Rome to Bari in about 4 hours. A car is the easiest way to explore.
gettingAround: Rent a car; regional trains link Bari, Polignano, Monopoli and the towns of the Itria Valley.
foodTip: Orecchiette with turnip tops, burrata, panzerotti, and raw seafood in Bari.
buyTip: Olive oil, ceramics from Grottaglie and taralli biscuits.

items.name: Alberobello
items.summary: A town of over a thousand trulli, whitewashed stone houses with cone roofs.
items.expect: Busy with day-trippers; souvenir shops fill some trulli.
items.tip: Stay overnight in a trullo.

items.name: Polignano a Mare
items.summary: A white town on the cliff edge above the Lama Monachile cove.
items.expect: The cove is tiny and busy in summer.
items.tip: Swim in the cove early morning.

items.name: Monopoli old town
items.summary: A walled fishing town with a castle and a harbour of blue boats.
items.tip: Eat seafood by the old port.

items.name: Ostuni
items.summary: The 'white city', a hilltop of whitewashed lanes and a cathedral.
items.tip: Watch the sunset from the walls.

items.name: Locorotondo
items.summary: A round hill town of white lanes overlooking trulli and vineyards.
items.tip: Taste the local white wine.
items.why: One of Italy's most beautiful villages.

items.name: Matera
items.summary: An ancient city of cave dwellings and rock churches carved into a ravine.
items.tip: Stay for the sassi lit up at night.
items.why: One of the world's oldest inhabited cities.

items.name: Lecce
items.summary: The 'Florence of the south', a city of honey-coloured Baroque churches.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by car or train.
items.tip: See the Basilica di Santa Croce.

items.name: Orecchiette
items.summary: Little ear-shaped pasta with turnip tops or tomato sauce.
items.expect: Women make it by hand in Bari's old town.
items.tip: Watch the pasta makers in Bari Vecchia.

items.name: Burrata
items.summary: Fresh mozzarella filled with cream, made in Puglia.
items.expect: Best eaten the day it's made.
items.tip: Buy it from a caseificio.

items.name: Panzerotti
items.summary: Fried half-moon pastries with tomato and mozzarella.
items.tip: Eat one hot.
